zone.source: Challenge description: Moon base atmosphere expected at 30% O2 or more and 10.2 psi or less

presets.label: Moon base
presets.note: Challenge reference atmosphere for a Moon base: 30% O2 or more at 10.2 psi or less.

presets.label: ISS / spacecraft
presets.note: Assumed Earth-normal cabin air (21% O2 at 14.7 psi). Verify before citing.

presets.label: Pressurized rover
presets.note: Challenge text puts pressurized rovers in the same intermediate atmosphere as the Moon base. Gravity depends on where it drives.

presets.label: Spacesuit boundary
presets.note: Challenge text: spacesuits use 100% O2 at 4.3 psi. The extreme corner of the map.

timeline.title: Apollo 1
timeline.text: A fire erupted during a pre-launch test in the oxygen-filled spacecraft and the crew died.
timeline.why: Why oxygen concentration is the first variable on our map.

timeline.title: Apollo 13
timeline.text: An oxygen tank exploded on the way to the Moon, endangering the crew.
timeline.why: Oxygen systems are a fire and explosion risk, not only a breathing resource.

timeline.title: Fire aboard Mir
timeline.text: An oxygen generator failure started a fire during joint operations that prepared for the International Space Station.
timeline.why: Detection and suppression in a station: the questions SAME and FLEX study.

timeline.title: Artemis II smoke alarm
timeline.text: Per the challenge text, the commander said a fire alarm gets your attention fast when you are about 80,000 miles from home.
timeline.why: Fire detection still matters on every crewed mission.

timeline.title: Moon base atmospheres
timeline.text: Planned habitats and pressurized rovers are expected at 30% O2 or more at lower pressure, which makes materials more flammable.
timeline.why: The map shows how little test data sits in that zone.

earth.title: A fire detector that tells smoke from dust
earth.summary: A smoke detector developed for the shuttle that discriminates between smoke and dust, so it gives fewer nuisance alarms. It has industrial uses, for example in mining.
earth.connection: SAME and SAME-R study smoke particles in microgravity, and DAFT reused one of their instruments for dust: the same smoke-versus-dust question.

earth.title: Firefighters' air tanks
earth.summary: Spacesuit technology adapted to improve firefighters' air tanks and breathing gear.
earth.connection: Spacesuits run on 100% oxygen at 4.3 psi, the far corner of the oxygen and pressure map in this platform.

earth.title: Fire attire
earth.summary: Spacesuit technology applied to improve firefighter clothing.
earth.connection: BASS, BASS-II and Saffire burn fabrics and plastics: the material flammability evidence behind protective-clothing choices.

earth.title: Fine-water-mist extinguishers
earth.summary: The challenge text notes that fine-water-mist extinguishers developed for the ISS have practical applications on Earth.
earth.connection: Suppression evidence in FLEX and BASS shows how extinguishing agents behave without buoyancy.
